question: The shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r}=\hat{i}+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j})$ and $\vec{r}=p\hat{j}+\hat{k}+\mu(\hat{i}+\hat{k})$ is $\sqrt{3}$ units, where $p>0$. Determine $p$ and establish that the corresponding pair of lines is skew.
explanation:
Applying the Shortest Distance Formula
Write the lines in the form $\vec{r}=\vec{a_1}+\lambda\vec{b_1}$ and $\vec{r}=\vec{a_2}+\mu\vec{b_2}$, where
$$\vec{a_1}=\hat{i},\quad \vec{b_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j},\quad \vec{a_2}=p\hat{j}+\hat{k},\quad \vec{b_2}=\hat{i}+\hat{k}$$
For two non-parallel lines, the shortest distance is
$$d=\frac{\left|\left(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}\right)\cdot\left(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}\right)\right|}{|\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}|}$$
Now,
$$\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}$$
and
$$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=-\hat{i}+p\hat{j}+\hat{k}$$
Therefore,
$$\left(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}\right)\cdot\left(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}\right)=-1-p-1=-(p+2)$$
Also,
$$|\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}|=\sqrt{1^2+(-1)^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{3}$$
Thus,
$$\sqrt{3}=\frac{|p+2|}{\sqrt{3}}$$
which gives
$$|p+2|=3$$
Hence, $p=1$ or $p=-5$. Since $p>0$,
$$p=1$$

Verification of Skewness
For $p=1$, the scalar triple product used in the coplanarity test is
$$\left(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}\right)\cdot\left(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}\right)=-3\ne0$$
Hence, the lines are not coplanar. Since their direction vectors $(1,1,0)$ and $(1,0,1)$ are not proportional, they are not parallel. Therefore, the lines are skew.

Final Result
The required value is $p=1$, and for this value the two lines are skew.

options.C: $p=1$; the scalar triple product is non-zero, so the lines are skew.
